==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|habba|habaa|haaba|haabaa}}

===Etymology===
{{bor+|en|ha|haba}}.

===Pronunciation===
{{rfp|en}}

===Interjection===
{{en-intj}}

# {{lb|en|Nigeria}} Expressing strong surprise, often mixed with disbelief or disapproval; ''you can't be serious!'', ''no way!''
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2020|author=Foluke Olayinka Unuabonah; Florence Oluwaseyi Daniel|title=Haba! Bilingual interjections in Nigerian English: A corpus-based study|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|volume=163|page=67|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2020.04.004|passage=Now candidates pay N1,000 to JAMB to print the result themselves. '''Haba'''. There should be some decency and fairness in "revenue generation".|footer=(quoting the Nigerian component of the International Corpus of English)}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2020|author=Foluke Olayinka Unuabonah; Florence Oluwaseyi Daniel|title=Haba! Bilingual interjections in Nigerian English: A corpus-based study|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|volume=163|page=69|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2020.04.004|passage=Nija women, wake up pleaaaaaaase and stand up for yourselves. '''Haba''', marriage should be about coming together to become one.|footer=(quoting a web post in the Nigerian component of the GloWbE corpus)}}
# {{lb|en|Nigeria}} Expressing other strong feelings, such as distress, pity, disgust or despair; occasionally positive surprise.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2020|author=Foluke Olayinka Unuabonah; Florence Oluwaseyi Daniel|title=Haba! Bilingual interjections in Nigerian English: A corpus-based study|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|volume=163|page=70|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2020.04.004|passage=Cos I'm so upset '''haba'''! Must people make money in such pity, terrible and sad situation like tht|footer=(quoting a web post in the Nigerian component of the GloWbE corpus)}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2020|author=Foluke Olayinka Unuabonah; Florence Oluwaseyi Daniel|title=Haba! Bilingual interjections in Nigerian English: A corpus-based study|journal=Journal of Pragmatics|volume=163|page=70|doi=10.1016/j.pragma.2020.04.004|passage='''Haba''' Nigerians! Where are we going?|footer=(quoting a web post in the Nigerian component of the GloWbE corpus)}}

====Usage notes====
* ''Haba'' is free-standing. It usually precedes the utterance it reacts to: 167 of 248 tokens in the Nigerian component of GloWbE precede it, and 81 follow it.
* It is often followed by an address term (''Haba Jade'', ''Haba, Achebe''), and occasionally preceded by ''but''.
* ''Haba'' is the usual spelling.
